advice: Abstain. The NN kernel needs 128 KiB of packed-A scratch to serve both 32-row halves across 512 K steps. Reducing it to 64 KiB requires changing scratch addressing and traversal; the proposed half-band approach overlaps the previously measured row-half-first traversal and has no demonstrated benefit. Reserving scratch once was also measured and not promoted. I have no distinct, legal scratch-lifetime change supported by the supplied evidence.
risks: The scratch reservation is a stack-pointer adjustment; the supplied evidence does not show separate initialization cost that can be removed. A new scratch layout or traversal would change multiple parts of the timed kernel, and noisy joint results would not identify a scratch-lifetime effect.
